Input Bar - Full Feature Guide

The input bar is the core entry point for chatting, with far more functionality than it appears:

- Plus menu (left): Tap to expand the tool panel - send images, files, select knowledge base documents, add prompt templates, enable drawing mode, delegate to other assistants, or restart context.

- Microphone (right): Tap to start voice input, release to convert speech to text (requires ASR configuration, see Chapter 4).

- Send button (when text exists): Paper airplane icon, tap to send.

- Stop button (while streaming with no new input): Red filled circle, tap to stop the current AI response.

- Enqueue button (while streaming with new input): Appears on the left - tap to queue your message without interrupting the current AI reply.

- Interject button (while streaming with new input): Arrow icon on the right - tap to interrupt and send your new message.

- Deep thinking toggle: Tap the brain icon to highlight and enable; tap again to disable. Long press to cycle thinking levels (low/medium/high/xhigh).

- Web search toggle: Tap the globe icon to highlight and enable; tap again to disable.

- Enter to send: Enable the "Enter to send" option in Settings. When on, press Enter to send directly, Shift+Enter for a new line.
Message Long-Press Menu & Forking

Long-press any message (yours or AI's) to open the action menu. Common options include:

- Copy: Copy the message text to clipboard.
- Regenerate: Tap on an AI message to generate a new reply that replaces the old one (the original is kept in history).
- Edit: Tap on your own message to modify and resend - a new branch grows from that point.
- Fork: Start an entirely new conversation branch from this message. The original conversation is untouched, letting you explore different directions.
- React: Add an Emoji reaction (like, heart, wow, etc.).
- Delete: Remove the message (optionally including all following messages).

These operations let you branch out in multiple directions within one conversation and backtrack anytime.
Conversation Management: Pin, Archive & Folders

On the chat list page, beyond new and delete, there are useful organization features:

- Pin conversations: Long-press or swipe left on a conversation, select Pin. Pinned conversations stay fixed at the top of the list for quick access.

- Archive conversations: Archive conversations you no longer need but don't want to delete. Archived chats are hidden from the main list and found under Archived. You can unarchive anytime.

- Folder categorization: Advanced users can create folders in Settings to group conversations by topic, e.g. Work, Study, Life, making batch management and lookup easier.

- History search: Type keywords in the search box at the top of the list to quickly locate all historical messages containing that keyword (cross-conversation search).

Proper organization keeps your Muse experience clean and tidy over long-term use.
Task Model Routing (Token Saver)

Settings → Task Routing lets you specify a cheap small model to handle tool calls (file reading, weather check, search, etc.) while the main model handles dialogue.

Why important? Tool calls consume tokens, and using expensive models for simple tasks is costly. With routing, routine tool calls use a cheap model (fraction of the price), while only complex dialogues use the powerful model, significantly reducing costs.

Beginners are also recommended to enable this — just pick an affordable reliable model (like deepseek-chat) as the tool model in settings.
Voice Input Setup & Usage

Voice input requires configuring a speech recognition (ASR) service before use in the chat page.

- Setup: Settings → Voice Settings, select an ASR provider (e.g. DashScope, Whisper), enter the corresponding API Key.

- Usage: Tap the microphone icon on the right of the input box on the chat page, speak and release, the system automatically converts speech to text. You can still edit the text before sending after recognition.

- Note: Recognition quality depends on the selected provider and your network environment. For first use, test the recognition effect in settings first, then use regularly once satisfied.

- Multilingual: Some providers support multilingual recognition; switch target language in settings.
Voice Conversation Mode & Voice Switching

Beyond voice input, Muse supports voice conversation mode (TTS reading aloud) and voice selection.

- Voice conversation: When enabled, the AI reads replies aloud using text-to-speech. Toggle in Settings → Voice Settings.

- Switch voice: Some providers support multiple TTS voices (male/female/different tones). Browse and select preferred voices in Settings → Voice Settings. The selected voice will be used for AI reply narration.

- Pronunciation quality: Depends on the TTS provider and selected voice model. Start with default voice to get familiar, then adjust per preference.

- Note: Voice conversation consumes extra tokens (text-to-speech). Confirm related costs before enabling.
Scheduled Tasks & Proactive Messages

Muse supports setting up scheduled tasks for the AI to proactively message you or perform actions at specified times.

- Setup path: Bottom of chat list page has a Scheduled Tasks entry, or configure in Settings → Task Management.

- Common use cases:
 - Push weather and today's to-dos every morning at 8 AM
 - Auto-summarize weekly conversation highlights every Sunday evening
 - Set reminders for specific events at designated times

- How to configure: Tap New Scheduled Task, select trigger time (one-time or recurring), fill in trigger content or prompt, save. The task auto-executes at the specified time and pushes results to you.

- View & manage: On the Tasks page you can see all scheduled tasks, with support for enabling/disabling/editing/deleting.
Tool Call Cards: Expand & Failure Feedback

When the AI calls tools (e.g. search, read file, execute command), a tool call card appears in the chat.

- Collapsed state: Card shows tool name icon + a Chinese summary (e.g. 'searched web for xxx'), giving instant clarity on what AI is doing.

- Expanded state: Tap the card to expand and see parameter key-value pairs, full result text, and previews of generated images/videos/files (if any).

- Running: Card shows a spinning progress indicator while processing.

- Failure feedback: If a tool call fails, the card uses a red error container background + error message. Tap to expand and see the specific error reason for troubleshooting.

- Links in results: If tool output contains file paths, they appear as attachment chips - tap to view or download directly.

Tool call cards let you see every step of AI's operation transparently and controllably.
Message Multi-Select Mode
Connections & Extensions (2.0)
Message channels: connect AI to Feishu / QQ

Settings → Message channels connects Muse to your IM.
- Feishu: create a custom app at open.feishu.cn, enable im:message, add the bot to a group; call GET /im/v1/chats in the API console to copy the chat_id (starts with oc_). Fill App ID / App Secret / chat_id in Muse.
- QQ: create a bot at bot.q.qq.com, fill AppID / AppSecret. Group or user openid appears automatically after the bot receives a message (WebServer must be reachable).
- Usage: say "send this to Feishu" and the AI calls the send tool (with approval).
- Receiving: pushed messages appear in the channel page under Recently received.
OAuth connectors: authorize external services

Settings → Connectors connects any OAuth2 service (GitHub, Notion, calendar apps...).
- Prepare: register an OAuth app in the provider console; set the redirect URI to io.zer0.muse://oauth/callback.
- Configure: fill authorize URL, token URL, scope, Client ID / Secret on the connector page and save.
- Connect: tap Connect, finish authorization in the system browser and return to Muse. Credentials are encrypted locally.
- Purpose: one shared authorization channel for future data features.
Interactive cards: from display to action

HTML cards in AI replies are now interactive.
- Buttons inside a card can send a message back to the AI (e.g. "confirm start"); the AI responds to it.
- Safety guard: a callback only works within 1.5s after your last tap, preventing automatic message spam.
- Save as artifact: tap the bookmark icon to keep the card as an artifact.
Skill packs and plugin panels

- Skill packs: tap the share icon on the Skills page to pack all your custom skills into one file and send it; importing it installs them in batch.
- Plugin panels: plugins declaring uiPanel show an "Open panel" entry with a custom UI (dashboards, reports...).
(Plugins are signed by their authors; trust is confirmed at install time.)
Web tasks: let AI browse for you
Webhook tunneling: let platforms reach your phone

Channel webhooks need the platform servers to reach your phone, but phones usually lack a public address.

- Recommended setup (computer as a relay): keep the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi; install a tunnel tool such as cloudflared on the computer and run cloudflared tunnel --url http://phone-ip:port; it prints a public URL like https://xxx.trycloudflare.com.

- Wiring: append /webhook/feishu or /webhook/qq to that public URL and fill it into the platform callback settings; once verified, incoming messages flow into the Muse inbox and can be handled by the channel auto-reply.

- Notes: temporary tunnel URLs change after restart, so update the platform config when that happens; keep both devices on the same network and the computer awake; security is covered by platform signatures — Ed25519 for QQ, challenge verification for Feishu.

The AI can now drive the built-in browser (headless, non-intrusive).
- Flow: first it "reads" the page (structured snapshot of links / buttons / inputs with numbers), then clicks or types by number to paginate, fill forms and collect data.
- Trigger: just say "open "site" and check "something""; for login-required sites, log in manually first and the AI reuses the session.
- Safety: clicks and typing go through approval; top-level navigation is blocked.

After long-pressing to enter multi-select mode, you can select multiple messages at once for batch operations.

- Entry: Long-press any message to enter multi-select mode; checkboxes appear on the left of all messages.

- Batch operations: After selecting multiple messages, perform batch copy, batch delete, etc. Some versions also support batch favorite.

- Exit: Tap the cancel button in the top-right corner, or tap blank area to exit multi-select mode and return to normal browsing.

Multi-select mode is highly efficient when handling large numbers of messages, saving significant time compared to operating one by one.
